Types of antacids

  • Aluminum hydroxide
  • Calcium salts
  • Magnesium salts
  • Sodium bicarbonate

Aluminum Hydroxide

Aluminum hydroxide work as antacids by neutralizing stomach acid and it also inhibit pepsin proteolytic activity leading to alleviation of heartburn, ulcer healing and pyloric spasm relief

In addition to its use as antacids; Aluminum hydroxide is also combined with sulfated polysaccharide sucrose octasulfate to form sucralfate (which help healing peptic ulcers by reducing pepsin and acid contact with the ulcer)

It is also used in treatment of hyperphosphatemia because of its ability to bind phosphate in the GI tract

Calcium carbonate

Calcium carbonate work as antacids by neutralizing stomach acid, they also inhibit pepsin proteolytic activity and increase lower esophageal sphincter tone

The calcium released work also to increase esophageal peristalsis pushing the acid in the stomach and providing relief from the heartburn symptoms

Calcium salts also bind dietary phosphate and prevent its absorption

Therapeutic uses

Antacids are over the counter meds and currently their use is restricted to relieving mild intermittent GERD (gives heartburn symptoms)

Previously antacids were the first line treatment for peptic ulcer disease, but when the PPIs got discovered, antacids stopped being used for PUD

Adverse effects

Calcium carbonate may lead to:

Hypercalcemia

Abdominal pain

Anorexia

Acid rebound

Nausea and vomiting

Flatulence

Dry mouth

Headache

Hypophosphatemia

Milk alkali syndrome

Antacids containing magnesium may cause diarrhea while antacids containing calcium or aluminum may cause constipation

Antacids overuse may lead to acid rebound

Aluminum is a heavy metal, its use in individuals with renal failure and infants is associated with increased risk of toxicity

Aluminum toxicity present as: osteopenia, microcytic anemia, neurotoxicity, osteomalacia, constipation, fecal impaction, nausea and vomiting, abdominal cramps, hypomagnesemia and hypophosphatemia

Milk alkali syndrome

Milk alkali syndrome is a triad of elevated calcium levels, metabolic alkalosis, and acute kidney injury

It is associated with consumption of large quantities of milk and calcium carbonate for peptic ulcer disease treatment especially in osteoporotic patients with CKD

If not treated, it may lead to AKI and metastatic calcification

Drug interactions

Antacids impair the absorption of acidic drugs (e.g. digoxin, chlorpromazine and isoniazid) leading to reduction in their blood concentrations and failure of therapy

Antacids can increase the absorption of some drugs (e.g. pseudoephedrine and levodopa) leading to potential toxicity and adverse effects

Antacids containing magnesium slats can bind to drugs like tetracycline and fluoroquinolone antibiotics preventing their absorption

Sodium bicarbonate increase urine PH, which can alter renal elimination of some drugs; leading to inhibition of elimination of basic drugs and increase elimination of acidic drugs
